records.name: Rhaenyra Targaryen
records.status_at_cutoff: Alive, in King's Landing, holding the Iron Throne after recovering Rhaena. Facing an empty treasury, food shortages, a hostile Faith and restive dragonseeds.
records.season_arc: Wins the capital in E2 and discovers governing is harder than conquering. Jace’s death, insolvency and repeated betrayal push her toward paranoia and increasingly coercive rule.
records.losses: Jace, Vermax, most of her treasury, confidence in Daemon, dragonseed loyalty
records.critical_discourse: D'Arcy's darkening performance is widely praised; critics argue the show swung from over-softening Rhaenyra to making her irrational too abruptly.
records.audience_reaction: GOODWILL DETERIORATING. The complaint is not that she is evil but that her decisions look self-destructive — alienating dragonseeds, mistrusting advisers, mishandling the city. 'Rhaenyra's downfall' is now a common video title. Viewers are actively arguing whether this is good tragedy or bad writing.

spoiler_scope.note: Verified screen knowledge ends with Season 3, Episode 7.

records.name: Daemon Targaryen
records.status_at_cutoff: Alive. Last confirmed at the Sheepstealer fight, having deliberately let the wounded dragon escape. Exact location after that scene is NOT established — do not place him.
records.season_arc: Military asset and increasingly imperial-minded co-ruler. Secretly protected Rhaena by murdering a shepherd and passing off the body as Sheepstealer’s rider; the deception is now exposed.
records.losses: Jace, political trust, many Gold Cloaks
records.critical_discourse: Some criticism that his season again detours into family/mystical material after S2 spent so long at Harrenhal.
records.audience_reaction: DEBATABLE. Viewers were divided on him, but E7 earned real credit: many noticed he could have had Caraxes finish Sheepstealer and deliberately chose not to, reading it as choosing his daughter over the obvious move.

spoiler_scope.note: Verified screen knowledge ends with Season 3, Episode 7.

records.name: Aemond Targaryen
records.status_at_cutoff: ALIVE but poisoned with nightshade by Alicent and collapsed at Harrenhal. There is NO on-screen death. His fate is the season’s biggest open question.
records.season_arc: Opens powerful enough to menace both factions and destroys the Strongs, then spends most of the season wounded and dependent on Alys Rivers. His need for maternal approval is made explicit and sexualised.
records.losses: Operational command, physical health, Vhagar's presence, Alicent's loyalty
records.critical_discourse: The Harrenhal slowdown and the Oedipal rewrite are heavily disputed; Mitchell’s vulnerable performance is often praised.
records.audience_reaction: MIXED BUT HIGHLY ENGAGED. 'Mommy issues' has become the shorthand for S3 Aemond. The Alys material works for viewers as gothic psychological horror, not romance. There is real fatigue about another Targaryen stuck at Harrenhal hallucinating.

spoiler_scope.note: Verified screen knowledge ends with Season 3, Episode 7.

records.name: Alicent Hightower
records.status_at_cutoff: Alive, at Harrenhal, having just poisoned Aemond as the price of Rhaenyra protecting Helaena.
records.season_arc: Delivers King's Landing to the Blacks by disabling its defences and flipping the Gold Cloaks, then fights to protect Helaena. Rhaenyra's price is Aemond's death, and she goes through with it.
records.losses: Political power, Otto, Aegon as an ally, Aemond’s trust, her freedom
records.critical_discourse: Possibly the season's most divisive characterisation: critics question whether poisoning her own son follows from two seasons of maternal motivation.
records.audience_reaction: THE WRITING IS THE TARGET, NOT THE ACTOR. The poisoning is the focal point of a 'they broke Alicent' argument. Crucially, viewers are sympathetic to Olivia Cooke and think she is excellent — they are unhappy with what the scripts ask her to sell. Do not mock the performance.

spoiler_scope.note: Verified screen knowledge ends with Season 3, Episode 7.

records.name: Aegon II Targaryen
records.status_at_cutoff: Alive, scarred and disabled, on the road with Tyland, newly re-emboldened after Sunfyre returned and killed the Black soldiers confronting him.
records.season_arc: The dethroned king spends most of the season humiliated and forced to confront his own failures. His road-trip with Larys and the Sunfyre reunion give him the clearest reversal of the season.
records.losses: King's Landing, the throne, physical mobility, much of his entitlement
records.critical_discourse: Glynn-Carney’s humanisation of Aegon is among the season’s most consistently praised performances.
records.audience_reaction: THE SEASON'S BIGGEST WINNER. Viewers who mocked him now name him a favourite. The wounded road story stripped the swagger and made him a person. You do not have to back him politically to enjoy watching him.

spoiler_scope.note: Verified screen knowledge ends with Season 3, Episode 7.

records.name: Helaena Targaryen
records.status_at_cutoff: Alive and pregnant, effectively a Black ward/prisoner in King's Landing, still protecting Jaehaera.
records.season_arc: Asserts agency by refusing Alicent’s attempt to end her pregnancy and refusing separation from Jaehaera. Her visions intensify while she keeps rejecting the warrior-dragonrider role.
records.losses: Jaehaerys (before S3), her freedom, most of her family structure
records.critical_discourse: Making her a noncombatant dragonrider is a significant adaptation debate; Saban’s performance and the Dreamfyre vision were well received.
records.audience_reaction: INTENSELY PROTECTED. Generates unusually little hostility. Enormous excitement about Dreamfyre finally appearing, and viewers are decoding her visions rather than dismissing them. The instinct is 'protect Helaena at all costs'.

spoiler_scope.note: Verified screen knowledge ends with Season 3, Episode 7.

records.name: Ormund Hightower
records.status_at_cutoff: Alive, controls Tumbleton, holds Corlys prisoner, and has secretly turned Ulf. A large Black northern host is closing on him.
records.season_arc: The Greens' most competent strategist: anti-Targaryen in rhetoric, entirely willing to exploit Daeron's Targaryen blood and dragon.
records.losses: Very little so far
records.critical_discourse: Norton widely praised; criticism that Ormund feels implausibly omniscient because too many covert operations succeed perfectly.
records.audience_reaction: LOVE TO HATE. 'I hate this man, give me more of this man.' People hate what he does to Daeron and enjoy watching him do it. Note the difference from Alicent criticism: nobody wants Ormund's scenes removed, they want to analyse them.

spoiler_scope.note: Verified screen knowledge ends with Season 3, Episode 7.

records.name: Daeron Targaryen
records.status_at_cutoff: Alive at Tumbleton, resisting Ormund’s attempts to make him a puppet king, with Gwayne acting as a counterweight.
records.season_arc: Forced by Ormund to execute Leo in E4. Caught between his Targaryen identity and Hightower upbringing, and increasingly recoiling from his own side.
records.losses: His innocence, and any illusion about what Ormund wants from him
records.critical_discourse: Broadly praised — gives the Greens an unusually sympathetic internal dissenter.
records.audience_reaction: A SUCCESS. Landed well with show-only viewers. Audiences particularly like his genuine affection for Tessarion set against Ormund's coldly instrumental view of dragons. Some book-reader complaints that he has been changed too much.

spoiler_scope.note: Verified screen knowledge ends with Season 3, Episode 7.

records.name: Hugh Hammer
records.status_at_cutoff: Alive and STILL BLACK-ALIGNED on screen. Tied to occupied Tumbleton through his wife Kat, who refuses to leave with him. Loyalty strained — but no defection has happened.
records.season_arc: His dragon makes him enormously powerful while Rhaenyra’s handling of the dragonseeds leaves him caught between duty and family.
records.losses: Domestic stability, Kat's trust
records.critical_discourse: Critics question why Kat refuses obvious chances to leave Tumbleton. Book-reader discourse about Hugh is heavily contaminated — do not pre-empt his choice.
records.audience_reaction: UNDER-DISCUSSED relative to Ulf. A suspense character rather than a fandom character — the conversation is about Kat, the dragonseeds and what he will choose, rather than about him.

spoiler_scope.note: Verified screen knowledge ends with Season 3, Episode 7.

records.name: Ulf the White
records.status_at_cutoff: Alive and SECRETLY TURNED TO THE GREENS in E7, won over by Ormund with respect, pleasure and the promise of Driftmark. CRITICALLY: nobody on Team Black knows. Rhaenyra and Daemon still count him and Silverwing as theirs. The audience knows; the characters do not.
records.season_arc: A lowborn rider desperate for status is belittled, restricted and finally struck by Daemon. Ormund exploits exactly those resentments.
records.losses: Loyalty to Rhaenyra; any trust in Black leadership
records.critical_discourse: One of the more successful causal rewrites — even critics hostile to the adaptation can see why THIS version of Ulf defects.
records.audience_reaction: SURPRISINGLY WELL LIKED. Obnoxious, but the show made his resentment comprehensible — 'Ulf's motives are completely understandable' is a common note. Viewers condemn the behaviour while buying the psychology.

spoiler_scope.note: Verified screen knowledge ends with Season 3, Episode 7.

records.name: Corlys Velaryon
records.status_at_cutoff: Alive but a PRISONER of Ormund at Tumbleton, missing a finger — sent to Alyn as proof.
records.season_arc: Survives the Gullet, finally acknowledges Addam and Alyn as his sons, clashes with Rhaenyra over legitimising them, then is abducted by Bold Jon Roxton.
records.losses: High Tide, fleet strength, Jace, his freedom, a finger
records.critical_discourse: Criticism centres on how implausibly easily such an experienced warlord is kidnapped.
records.audience_reaction: SYMPATHETIC, though viewers find it implausible that so experienced a warlord was kidnapped so easily.

spoiler_scope.note: Verified screen knowledge ends with Season 3, Episode 7.

records.name: Addam of Hull
records.status_at_cutoff: Alive and an active Black dragonrider; helped contain Sheepstealer and escort the queen’s retreat.
records.season_arc: Stays loyal despite Rhaenyra refusing to grant him the Velaryon name, becoming one of her most dependable riders.
records.losses: Security of Driftmark; an uncomplicated relationship with Corlys
records.critical_discourse: Much less controversial than Hugh or Ulf; his loyalty increasingly contrasts with Rhaenyra’s mistrust of dragonseeds.
records.audience_reaction: QUIETLY LIKED. His loyalty reads well against Rhaenyra's mistrust of the dragonseeds.

spoiler_scope.note: Verified screen knowledge ends with Season 3, Episode 7.

records.name: Alyn of Hull
records.status_at_cutoff: Alive, commanding Velaryon forces, and has just received proof of Corlys’s captivity.
records.season_arc: Kills Sharako Lohar at the Gullet, confronts Corlys over decades of neglect, and grows closer to Baela.
records.losses: High Tide’s security; an uncomplicated relationship with his father
records.critical_discourse: Salim’s Gullet material is praised, especially his rage when Corlys appears to fall.
records.audience_reaction: WELL RECEIVED, especially his rage at the Gullet when Corlys appears to fall.

spoiler_scope.note: Verified screen knowledge ends with Season 3, Episode 7.

records.name: Rhaena Targaryen
records.status_at_cutoff: Alive, returned to King's Landing with Rhaenyra after her secret was exposed. Sheepstealer is wounded and gone.
records.season_arc: Gets what she desperately wanted — becoming a dragonrider — but Sheepstealer’s uncontrolled intervention helps cause Jace’s death. Daemon hid her secret until Rhaenyra found out.
records.losses: Jace, safety in the Vale, and now Sheepstealer
records.critical_discourse: One of S3’s most disputed adaptation choices, and after E7 a large wave of fan sympathy for Sheepstealer.
records.audience_reaction: POLARIZED — and notably less liked than her dragon. Some credit her finally getting agency; a substantial contingent blames her for dragging Sheepstealer into a war he had no part in. Rule of thumb: Rhaena is a debate, Sheepstealer is applause.

spoiler_scope.note: Verified screen knowledge ends with Season 3, Episode 7.

records.name: Baela Targaryen
records.status_at_cutoff: Alive, reconciled with Rhaena, still one of Rhaenyra’s functioning riders.
records.season_arc: Survives the Gullet and develops a closer relationship with Alyn.
records.losses: Jace, her betrothed; High Tide’s security
records.critical_discourse: Some find the Alyn romance under-developed; others welcome Baela having a life beyond being Jace’s fiancée.
records.audience_reaction: LIKED. Some find the Alyn romance under-developed; others are glad she has a life beyond being Jace's fiancée.

spoiler_scope.note: Verified screen knowledge ends with Season 3, Episode 7.

records.name: Alys Rivers
records.status_at_cutoff: Alive at Harrenhal, standing over the poisoned Aemond, and in possession of a hidden clutch of dragon eggs.
records.season_arc: Reverses Aemond’s power dynamic entirely — healer, mystic, confidante and finally lover, while hiding dragon eggs.
records.losses: Nothing clear this season
records.critical_discourse: Rankin’s uncanny performance is praised; the Aemond romance has enthusiastic fans and viewers exhausted by another Harrenhal vision-loop.
records.audience_reaction: DIVISIVE BUT COMPELLING. Rankin's uncanny performance is praised; the Aemond material splits between enthusiasm and Harrenhal fatigue.

spoiler_scope.note: Verified screen knowledge ends with Season 3, Episode 7.

records.name: Mysaria
records.status_at_cutoff: Alive in King's Landing as Rhaenyra's spymaster and intimate partner.
records.season_arc: Her network becomes central to Rhaenyra’s government, but she conceals information and increasingly mixes influence with intimacy. She caught Alicent and Helaena attempting to flee.
records.losses: Her image of dispassionate control
records.critical_discourse: Criticism focuses on inconsistent competence and the abruptness of her renewed intimacy with Rhaenyra.
records.audience_reaction: ONE OF THE CLEAREST AUDIENCE LOSERS — but the complaint is screen time, not the character. 'The fact Mysaria gets more scenes than Aegon is criminal.' The argument is that the Rhaenyra/Mysaria material crowds out the war, Aegon and the dragons. Some viewers do like the chemistry.

spoiler_scope.note: Verified screen knowledge ends with Season 3, Episode 7.

records.name: Larys Strong
records.status_at_cutoff: Alive but has ABANDONED Aegon and Tyland rather than face the confrontation. Destination not established.
records.season_arc: Becomes Aegon’s brutally honest caretaker on the road — a pairing that humanises both — then chooses survival when it gets dangerous.
records.losses: King's Landing power base and control of events
records.critical_discourse: Aegon/Larys is repeatedly singled out as one of S3’s most entertaining relationships.
records.audience_reaction: ENJOYED. The Aegon/Larys/Tyland road story is a strong approval area, and Larys finally snapping at Aegon was called 'so damn satisfying'.

spoiler_scope.note: Verified screen knowledge ends with Season 3, Episode 7.

records.name: Gwayne Hightower
records.status_at_cutoff: Alive at Tumbleton, increasingly opposed to Ormund and protective of Daeron. Exposed a fake Baratheon assassination attempt.
records.season_arc: His horror at Criston’s moral collapse grows until he abandons Cole’s doomed army, then becomes the counterweight to Ormund.
records.losses: Army comrades, Criston, faith in the campaign
records.critical_discourse: His moral disgust gives the Green ground war a necessary internal opposition.
records.audience_reaction: LIKED as the Green side's conscience.

spoiler_scope.note: Verified screen knowledge ends with Season 3, Episode 7.

records.name: Tyland Lannister
records.status_at_cutoff: Alive, revealed to have survived the Gullet, and staying with Aegon after volunteering to stand beside him.
records.season_arc: Rejoins Aegon and Larys on the road; central to the unresolved mystery of the missing royal gold.
records.losses: The royal treasury he was responsible for
records.critical_discourse: Part of the Aegon/Larys/Tyland trio widely enjoyed as unexpected comic-human relief.
records.audience_reaction: ENJOYED as part of the Aegon/Larys/Tyland trio.

spoiler_scope.note: Verified screen knowledge ends with Season 3, Episode 7.

records.name: Roderick Dustin
records.status_at_cutoff: Alive, commanding the Winter Wolves, closing on the Hightower position at Tumbleton.
records.season_arc: Arrives as the aged, death-seeking commander of the Winter Wolves and helps destroy Criston’s force at the Butcher’s Ball.
records.losses: Men in the campaign
records.critical_discourse: Flanagan’s dry, brutal veteran performance is a well-liked addition.
records.audience_reaction: WELL LIKED. The dry, brutal veteran is a popular addition.

spoiler_scope.note: Verified screen knowledge ends with Season 3, Episode 7.

records.name: Oscar Tully
records.status_at_cutoff: Alive, co-commanding the Riverlands force closing on Tumbleton.
records.season_arc: Co-leads the coalition that annihilates Criston Cole’s army at the Butcher’s Ball.
records.losses: Men in the campaign
records.audience_reaction: POSITIVE but lower profile.

spoiler_scope.note: Verified screen knowledge ends with Season 3, Episode 7.

records.name: Alysanne Blackwood
records.status_at_cutoff: Alive with the Black river host. Known as Black Aly.
records.season_arc: Personally fired the three arrows that killed Criston Cole at the Butcher’s Ball — confirmed by Shapero after the episode.
records.critical_discourse: Forbes’s initial recap called the killer an unnamed northern archer; the actor’s later interview identifies Black Aly. Treat Black Aly as canon.
records.audience_reaction: A POINT OF INTEREST since it emerged she personally shot Criston Cole.

spoiler_scope.note: Verified screen knowledge ends with Season 3, Episode 7.

records.name: Bold Jon Roxton
records.status_at_cutoff: Alive; Ormund’s operative, having successfully kidnapped Corlys.
records.season_arc: Executes the abduction of Corlys Velaryon on Ormund’s behalf.
records.audience_reaction: LOW PROFILE.

spoiler_scope.note: Verified screen knowledge ends with Season 3, Episode 7.

records.name: Kat
records.status_at_cutoff: Alive in occupied Tumbleton, refusing to leave with Hugh.
records.season_arc: Sexually assaulted by a Hightower soldier in E4; her brother Leo was then executed by Daeron for striking the man while defending her. She has since refused to flee with Hugh.
records.losses: Her brother Leo; her safety
records.critical_discourse: Critics question why she refuses obvious opportunities to leave the occupied town.
records.audience_reaction: SYMPATHETIC, though viewers question why she will not leave Tumbleton.

spoiler_scope.note: Verified screen knowledge ends with Season 3, Episode 7.

records.name: Grand Maester Orwyle
records.status_at_cutoff: Alive in King's Landing, serving whichever regime holds it.
records.season_arc: Intervened to stop Jasper Wylde’s assault on Alicent and had him arrested. Caught between regimes.
records.losses: Any pretence of neutrality
records.audience_reaction: LOW PROFILE.

spoiler_scope.note: Verified screen knowledge ends with Season 3, Episode 7.

records.name: Torrhen Manderly
records.status_at_cutoff: Alive as far as E7 establishes. His exact position late in the season is NOT re-established — do not invent a battlefield location for him.
records.season_arc: A northern representative in Rhaenyra’s expanding coalition and her governance discussions.
records.losses: Nothing depicted
records.critical_discourse: Far less developed than Roddy Dustin.
records.audience_reaction: LOW PROFILE.

spoiler_scope.note: Verified screen knowledge ends with Season 3, Episode 7.
